intents.name: Cache Locality and Data Reuse
intents.description: Improve cache efficiency by tiling the convolution computation to fit working sets in L1/L2 cache and maximize data reuse across iterations.
intents.rationale: 2D convolution exhibits poor cache locality due to large strides through input and output tensors. Tiling output spatial dimensions and input channels into cache-friendly blocks reduces memory traffic and increases arithmetic intensity, critical on Broadwell with limited L3 bandwidth.

transformations.name: Tiling
transformations.description: Partition the convolution computation into rectangular tiles over output spatial dimensions (OH, OW) and input/output channels (C, F) to fit intermediate working sets in L1/L2 cache.
transformations.rationale: Reduces memory bandwidth pressure by reusing filter weights and input activations across multiple output elements; enables effective use of the 32KB L1d and 256KB L2 per core on Broadwell.

transformations.name: Loop Interchange
transformations.description: Reorder nested loops (e.g., prioritize innermost loops over spatial or channel dimensions) to improve memory access patterns and cache line utilization.
transformations.rationale: Convolution loop nests can exhibit poor locality if traversed in suboptimal order; reordering loops to match the memory layout of tensors reduces cache misses and TLB pressure.

intents.name: SIMD Vectorization and Instruction-Level Parallelism
intents.description: Expose data parallelism to AVX2 vector units by restructuring the computation to operate on aligned, contiguous data and eliminate scalar bottlenecks.
intents.rationale: Convolution kernels are compute-intensive and benefit significantly from 256-bit SIMD (AVX2); vectorizing the innermost loops over spatial or channel dimensions can yield 4–8× speedup on FP64 workloads while hiding latency.

transformations.name: Vectorization
transformations.description: Transform innermost loops (typically over output channels F or spatial dimensions) into SIMD-friendly form suitable for code generation targeting AVX2 vector instructions.
transformations.rationale: Direct vectorization of linalg.conv_2d_nchw_fchw or its lowered form exposes parallelism to the 8-wide (FP32) or 4-wide (FP64) AVX2 pipeline; reduces scalar loop overhead and improves ILP.

transformations.name: Layout Transformation
transformations.description: Reformat tensor layouts (e.g., NCHW → blocked/packed layouts) to align data access patterns with vector width and memory alignment requirements.
transformations.rationale: Convolution tensors in standard NCHW layout may not be conducive to aligned vector loads; transforming to a packed or blocked layout (e.g., NCHW → NC(H×W) or NC(8,8,C,4) for 8×8 tiles with 4-wide channels) enables efficient gather/broadcast and reduces alignment penalties.

intents.name: Coarse-Grain Parallelism and NUMA Awareness
intents.description: Distribute independent iterations across the 28 CPU cores while respecting NUMA topology to maximize throughput and minimize cross-socket traffic.
intents.rationale: On a 28-core Broadwell system with 2 NUMA sockets, naive parallelization risks imbalance and remote memory access; careful distribution over batch (N), spatial (OH, OW), or output channel (F) dimensions with NUMA-aware memory allocation is essential for scalable performance.

transformations.name: Parallelization
transformations.description: Parallelize independent outer loops (e.g., batch dimension N, output spatial dimensions OH/OW, or output channel F) across worker threads using a coarse-grain loop distribution strategy.
transformations.rationale: Convolution has abundant parallelism in batch, spatial, and channel dimensions; distributing these across 28 cores (avoiding oversubscription and false sharing) provides near-linear speedup for throughput-bound workloads.

transformations.name: Memory Allocation and Data Layout Strategy
transformations.description: Align tensor allocation and loop blocking to NUMA boundaries and socket-local caches to minimize cross-socket traffic and remote memory latency.
transformations.rationale: Large tensors (e.g., feature maps of shape N×F×OH×OW) may span multiple NUMA nodes; explicit NUMA-aware blocking or allocation strategy reduces off-socket memory accesses and improves scalability on multi-socket systems.

intents.name: Operator Fusion and Intermediate Materialization Reduction
intents.description: Fuse adjacent operations and reduce temporary buffer allocation by combining computations to decrease memory bandwidth and improve cache reuse.
intents.rationale: Convolution followed by activation or normalization layers is common in neural networks; fusing these operations eliminates intermediate tensor materialization and reduces memory traffic, especially critical for bandwidth-limited workloads.

transformations.name: Operator Fusion
transformations.description: Fuse the convolution operation with subsequent elementwise operations (e.g., ReLU, bias addition) into a single kernel to avoid redundant memory reads/writes of intermediate results.
transformations.rationale: Elementwise fusion reduces bandwidth by keeping intermediate results in registers or cache; typical fusion patterns (conv + ReLU, conv + bias) are ubiquitous in ML inference and can provide 20–40% speedup.

transformations.name: Loop Fusion
transformations.description: Merge nested loops across producer-consumer operation pairs to amortize loop overhead and improve data locality.
transformations.rationale: If convolution is followed by an independent tensor operation (e.g., transpose, normalization), fusing their loops reduces register spills and allows efficient pipelining on modern superscalar CPUs.

intents.name: Low-Level Loop Optimization and Register Efficiency
intents.description: Refine loop structure, unrolling, and register allocation to minimize loop overhead, hide latency, and reduce spills on the CPU pipeline.
intents.rationale: Convolution kernels often have high trip counts and instruction-level parallelism; careful loop unrolling, peeling, and jamming can hide FP64 latency (typically 3–5 cycles on Broadwell) and improve throughput by increasing in-flight instructions.

transformations.name: Loop Unrolling
transformations.description: Unroll innermost loops (over channels, spatial dimensions, or kernel height/width) by a factor determined by available ILP and register budget to reduce loop overhead and increase instruction density.
transformations.rationale: Reduces loop branch and increment overhead; increases the ratio of arithmetic operations to loop control, improving CPU pipeline efficiency and FP unit utilization on deep pipelines like Broadwell.

transformations.name: Peeling and Jamming
transformations.description: Peel loop boundaries (e.g., handle unaligned iterations separately) and jam independent loop bodies to minimize mispredictions and improve register allocation.
transformations.rationale: Separates aligned fast-path from edge cases, enabling aggressive optimization on the main loop; jamming increases instruction-level parallelism by exposing multiple independent operations to out-of-order execution.
